Heard Sri C.V.Nagesh, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri B.N.Jagadeesha, learned Additional State Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.1 and Sri Sandesh J.
Chouta, learned senior counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
 3.

Facts, in brief, germane are as follows: -
 3.1.
It is the averment in the petition that several crimes are registered against the 2nd respondent between the years 2012 to 2020.
Additionally, a complaint is also registered in the year 2022 against one Kishore Kumar B.K. and several other accused persons which becomes a crime in crime No.356 of 2022.
This Court in W.P.No.2071 of 2023 quashes the proceedings against Kishore  4 Kumar B.K. but rejects the petition for quashing against the other accused for the aforesaid crime.
The Special Leave Petition filed before the Apex Court challenging the order of this Court in W.P.No.2071 of 2023, comes to be withdrawn.
Further, on 18-07- 2023, the said Kishore Kumar B.K. files a complaint for criminal defamation against the 2nd respondent - present complainant and the petitioner herein.
The issue in the lis is not with regard to the crimes registered against the 2nd respondent or the other accused.

The issue now is with regard to a complaint that comes to be registered before the concerned Court on 24-04-2024 by the 2nd respondent in P.C.R.No.152 of 2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 365, 384, 388, 420 read with Section 34 of the IPC,

It is the allegation of the petitioner that this complaint was filed at the instance of the said Kishore Kumar B.K.
 3.2.
Several allegations are made against the accused in the complaint concerning alleged acts of M/s Sanchaya Land and Estate Private Limited.

sentences.text: The petitioner is alleged to be the owner of the said Company and has indulged himself in several illegalities.
The  5 concerned Court refers the matter for investigation.
Reference of the matter for investigation is what has driven the petitioner to this Court in the subject petition.

4. The learned senior counsel Sri C.V.Nagesh appearing for the petitioner would restrict his submission to the reference order of the concerned Court contending that the order of reference must bear application of mind.
He would take this Court through the order, to contend that it does not bear any application of mind as to why the matter is referred for investigation.
It is his submission that the complaint runs into several pages, as if it is a public interest litigation pending between the parties.

5. The learned senior counsel Sri Sandesh J. Chouta representing the 2nd respondent/complainant would refute the submissions in contending that the order of reference need not bear application of mind.

It is only referred for commencement of Sri Ravipati Vijay Tata vs The State Of Karnataka on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155472791/
4 investigation at the hands of the jurisdictional Police.

7. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the respective learned counsel and have perused the material on record.
8. The afore-narrated contentions lie in a narrow compass.
The private complaint is registered and the matter is referred for investigation.
The petitioner is before the Court.
Therefore, it is necessary to notice the complaint and the order of reference.

sentences.text: From the perusal of the complaint, the same is annexed  with the affidavit of the complainant and also an information has  been given as per Section 154(3) of Cr.P.C. to the  Superintendent of Police.

Therefore, on this score alone, the petition deserves to succeed, albeit in part, as the submissions made by the learned senior counsel, Sri C.V. Nagesh are also restricted to the order of reference and the order of reference quoted hereinabove undoubtedly depict blatant non- application of mind.
